correctness.rationale: For every finite connected noncomplete unweighted strongly regular graph, its three-dimensional adjacency algebra gives two explicit off-diagonal classes. Exact scalar identities R′(z)=-24((z²-15)²+375)/Q(z)²<0 and ((R(z)-1)/z)′=2(z⁴+120z²+1200z+3600)/Q(z)²>0 imply positive coefficient gamma and negative secant d. Nonedges have T_ij=mu gamma>0 and edges T_ij=-d+mu gamma>0 at all h>0. Spectral projector ranks make each diagonal F(h)=[1+fR(ah)+gR(bh)]/v, with strictly negative derivative, F(0)=1, limit (2-v)/v<0. Hence exactly one positive root gives the sharp [0,H] interval, with spectral norm 1 independently. The standalone exact symbolic/rational checker replayed successfully and verified 2,361 matrix entries; samples are corroboration, not the general proof. All normalization and boundary cases h=0,h=H,h>H were assessed.

originality.rationale: The primary finite-state Padé literature gives general positivity failures or nonsharp sufficient conditions rather than a full sixth-order [3/3] Gauss sign classification on all noncomplete strongly regular graphs. A published [2/2] Markov result concerns fourth-order rational stability on different operators. Earlier mathematical results on sixth-order Gauss complete multipartite graphs only cover a restricted subclass of noncomplete strongly regular graphs and cannot imply primitive Petersen/triangular-graph cases. value.rationale: Spectral A-stability alone does not maintain positivity of diffusion states. This natural large graph family has only three Laplacian eigenvalues but a nontrivial rational completed step. The finding identifies all potential negative coefficients globally, proves off-diagonal strict positivity for every positive step, gives a single sharp graph-parameter root for the precise diagonal loss of positivity, and demonstrates it on primitive strongly regular networks beyond existing complete-multipartite cases. It is an exact structural invariant of a canonical numerical integrator, not a routine sample or negligible bound improvement.
